rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window of all 10 compounds and identify critical pairs. The moderate gradient duration and temperature provide a useful baseline for subsequent slope and selectivity tests.
Halve the gradient duration to reduce the time penalty while testing how the critical pairs respond to slope. The initial run has enough resolution margin to justify substantial acceleration.
Keep the fast gradient and raise temperature to test selectivity changes in the crowded middle peaks. This isolates the temperature effect while aiming to preserve the zero time penalty.

A slightly shallower gradient should improve the crowded middle region, while 55 C may avoid the near-coelution seen at 60 C. The modest duration increase should keep the last peak close to the zero-time-penalty window.

Injection 4 already achieved the maximum CRF, so retain it as the best method. Slightly reducing gradient steepness may increase the narrow resolution margins while keeping the last peak within the zero-time-penalty window.

The maximum CRF is already secured; test a slightly higher starting organic fraction for an alternative optimum. This changes the gradient window and may improve the critical-pair margins while shortening retention, with particular attention to early-peak separation.

Reduce the endpoint from injection 6 to make the gradient shallower and recover resolution of the limiting pair. This may retain its improved separation of the other critical pair while keeping the time penalty at zero; injection 4 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

One further decrease in gradient steepness should lift the limiting pair above R = 1.5 while preserving separation of the other critical pair. The last peak is projected near 8 minutes, potentially yielding another maximum-score method with slightly better resolution margins.

Test the shorter-duration neighbor of the maximum-score method to locate its fast-gradient boundary at 55 C. Comparison with injections 2 and 3 also completes a temperature-selectivity check at this slope; retain injection 4 if resolution falls below target.

Test the upper-temperature neighbor of injection 4 while holding its gradient fixed. This establishes whether the maximum-score method tolerates a 5 C increase or whether the middle-pair selectivity requires 55 C.

Lower the endpoint one grid step from injection 21 to test the shallow-slope edge of the maximum-score region. The last peak is projected just below 9 minutes, while the limiting pair should remain close to baseline resolution.
